title: Opt-Out
text: “Huh…?”

“Right. So, the problem is that the Shield Hero can’t fight monsters on his own. That’s why I’m planning to buy you and have you attack in his place. It’s a selfish reason, and you might not trust me, but I hope you’ll come to understand, little by little.”

Keel’s eyes darted around as he took a few steps back. To me, he looks like nothing more than a little piglet, but he is a Demi-Human, after all. He’ll likely bow down before the authority of my Father, who is renowned as the Shield Hero.
“It’s okay if you don’t trust me yet. Trust isn’t something you can force on someone. But you’d better equip yourself with weapons if you want to survive from here on out.”
My Father showed my dad the money he had left. Of course, since he’s entrusted me with the seed money for my peddling business, there isn’t much left.
“I want to buy some gear for this kid.”
“Got it, An-chan. If that’s the reason, I’ll help out too. Come on over here. I’ll pick out some decent gear for you.”
My dad told Keel to show him his hand, and Keel did just that.
“I’d recommend a dagger for this kid. Well, it’s good for a beginner, but I think something like this will feel just right.”
“Got it. For now, I’d like you to pick out a weapon that seems usable… and some armor that looks easy to move in.”
“Got it.”
And so, the old man gave Keel a dagger and some armor. Though, maybe because of his level, they’re a bit cheap.

“Well, this will do for now. Giving him something that doesn’t fit him properly could lead to injury. If you feel the damage output is too low, just go to the weapon shop and buy a new one whenever you need to.”
“Got it.”
“Oink…”

I see—it’s not necessarily true that higher-performance weapons are always better. Since I’ve always used this spear, I hadn’t realized that. …Come to think of it, even with Legendary Weapons, you start by using the weaker ones first and work your way up as your level increases, so Father’s words are probably right. Well, I suppose that wraps up my conversation with Father?
“Next is me, then.”
“Hm? Does Spear-chan have something to ask as well?”
“I’d like to borrow the back room of the shop for a bit.”
“Again? What are you up to this time?”
“I’d like you to come along, too.”
“Well… fine.”
Leaving my father and the others behind, I went to the back of the weapon shop with my dad.
“What on earth is going on?”
“Just watch and see.”
I pulled out a bunch of equipment from the spear—items that looked useful from the monster we’d defeated last night.
“W-what!?”
My dad let out a cry when he saw the equipment coming out of the spear.

“It’s a drop from the Weapons skill. Now, here’s the thing: next time you’re getting new gear for Father, I’d like you to mix some of this in—making it look like you made it yourself—to make the rest seem weaker.”
“Well… I can hold onto it for An-chan and the others for a while… but why?”
“If you find out, your life will be in danger.”

After all, if the fact that my Father and the others are actually strong is revealed too early, assassins will show up. Since Father is already on his guard, I thought maybe having my dad modify the gear would make it look weaker.
“That’s a pretty wild story. Hey.”
“As a reward, I’ll give you the gear inside this.”
“Hold on…”
My dad checks the gear I dropped.
“There’s some pretty decent gear mixed in here… It’d fetch a hefty price if I sold it. Oh well… I guess I could dismantle it, and if it helps An-chan and the others, it’s not such a bad deal.”
“Count on me.”
“Sure thing.”
With that, the groundwork is mostly done. I return from the back of the shop and exchange a nod with my Father.
“Well, I think I’ll be heading out soon.”
For now, I’ll just focus on leveling up Yuki and Sakura until we meet up again.
“See you later. I’m going to go level up with Keel. Well… I probably won’t go anywhere too tough, though.”
“Hahaha, I hope you do your best.”
“Good luck, An-chan and the others.”

After my father-in-law saw us off, we each went our separate ways. I wandered freely from the castle town toward yet another village, casually defeating monsters along the way to provide meals for Yuki-chan and the others.

My goal this time is to really level up Sakura-chan and the others… but the problem is that an envoy from Siltvelt will be coming to my Father to recruit him. Well, since I’ve already explained the situation to my Father in advance, I’m sure he’ll turn them down. So I just kept strolling along the highway, carefree as ever.
Two days later.
“Kue!”
Yuki-chan is growing by leaps and bounds and will soon take on her Filolial Queen form.
“Gua!”

Sakura-chan, a day behind, has also grown into the form of Filolial-sama. Today was the day I was planning to casually run into my Father again. I rode on Yuki-chan’s back and returned to the town below Melromarc Castle.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun. It’s been two days.”
“That’s right. What a coincidence.”
“Thanks to Kou—the one you lent me, Motoyasu-kun—I’ve been saved in more ways than one.”
Acting a bit contrived, but insisting it was a purely chance encounter, we met up. Like Yuki-chan, Kou has also transformed into a Filolial King.
“How about it? Want to catch up and take a breather?”
“Sounds good. So, how much progress have you all made, Father?”
I look at my Father, Keel, and Kou. They don’t seem much different from the day before yesterday, though Keel looks a bit neater now.
“Oink! Oo-oo-oo!”
I have no idea what he’s saying. Hurry up and transform into a dog so you can speak human language. Oh? It’s a bit odd for a dog to transform and speak human language, isn’t it?
“I’m probably Level 7 right now. Keel-kun is Level 8. Kou is… around Level 10, I guess.”
Wary of prying eyes, my Father lied about Kou’s level.
“It’s much the same here, isn’t it?”
“So Filolials grow in unusual ways when raised by a hero, huh? That really surprised me. Plus, they’re so fast when you ride on their backs!”
“That’s the nature of a Filolial-sama, you see. Kou, thank you so much for protecting your Father.”
“Que!”
“Boo-boo!”
“Yeah. You did a great job too, Keel.”

My Father patted Keel on the head. It seems Keel’s attitude has softened quite a bit in just a few days. As expected of my Father, who is also one of the foremost slave handlers. It reminds me of the slaves back in my old village.
“Oh, right. An envoy from Siltvelt came by yesterday.”
“I see… And what happened?”
“They asked me to come to their country, but I refused, saying I couldn’t trust them.”

The Father said this in a rather loud voice, as if the near-trap set by the country had left him traumatized. Melromarc views Siltvelt as a threat, so he was surely under surveillance at that very moment. Given that, Melromarc will likely conclude that the Father trusts only a select few.

Melromarc’s people must have breathed a sigh of relief. After all, it would be a problem if my Father were to go to Siltvelt. As long as he remains within Melromarc’s borders, they’ll be lulled into a false sense of security—believing they can kill him sooner or later—and since they perceive my Father and his group as weak, their vigilance will likely wane.
Then my Father leaned in close to my ear and whispered.
“So, I’d like your help with a few things, and I’m planning to talk to you again today, Motoyasu-kun. Will you come?”
I nodded silently.
“Come to think of it, I got an invitation too.”
I don’t remember which country it was, but I received an invitation asking if I’d come—the same kind I recall getting in the first world. Back then, Crimson Swine butted in, so I didn’t respond.
“I turned it down, too. All right, I’ll go.”

Well, either way, I probably turned it down because I’d convinced myself I was comfortable in the first world. Partly due to my knowledge of the game, I’d also convinced myself that the other country was inefficient. Renzou and Itsuki probably thought something similar. Looking back now, we were being kept in the dark so they could conveniently exploit us heroes for their own purposes.
